affected_targets.heading: ## Requested vs Effective Account Binding Rules

exact_missing_items: HITL now contains two contract eras: older request-local (HITLRequest with tier_id, tier_type, allowed_actions[]) and newer runtime-facing (waiting_approval as blocked overlay, allowed_action_ids[], cmd.runtime.*)
Move approval anchoring onto canonical runtime identity: run_id, node_id, blocked_sequence, attempt_id?, plus execution-unit context refs
Add an explicit approval-scope field or object, likely approval_scope_key, so reusable approvals and one-off blocked-episode approvals cannot bleed together
Add durable approver identity fields to approval/rejection records/events so audit/history can explain who approved or declined
Deprecated allowed_actions[] is compatibility-only and MUST NOT appear in new canonical schemas
Identity semantics across docs must converge on OperationalIdentity block as the canonical snapshot
requested_account_id must always be accompanied by requested_account_binding (none / preferred / required) to clarify what failure mode applies when the requested account is unavailable
effective_account_id must always be present (may equal the default) and never absent from any record that involves a provider/model call
Introduce execution_unit_context as the canonical runtime-facing context object and make TierContext explicitly derived or compatibility-only

Canonical execution_unit_context minimum shape: project_id, run_id, thread_id?, feature_seam_id?, work_package_id?, node_id, attempt_id?, blocked_sequence?, replan_generation, execution_role, scheduler_lane, manual_priority?, safe_point_id?, remediation lineage refs, lane_id?, worktree_id?, workspace_ref, snapshot_ref?, requested/effective runtime identity, runtime state hooks
Refactor orchestrator-subagent-integration.md so selector and hook APIs consume: canonical execution-unit refs for truth and a smaller derived selection/decomposition object for heuristics
Make execution_role part of the canonical attempt packet in Contracts_V0.md and storage-plan.md
Define operational_identity as a separate optional field family for receipts, artifacts, and side-effect-bearing attempt/tool records
execution_role and operational_identity solve different problems and should not be merged
Multi-Account.md still has no durable account.switched / switch-episode family
provider_accounts.run_snapshot still stores only an opaque policy_hash rather than a queryable policy version/ref
no canonical role enum or actor_kind / execution_role field exists to support role-by-provider and role-by-account overrides consistently across docs
On restart, the runtime restores current unresolved blocked episodes from canonical blocked/runtime records/projections
The scheduler then emits a scheduler pass with wake_reason = startup_recovered; that startup-recovery pass does not mint new blocked episodes by itself; it rehydrates existing unresolved episodes
Executor_Protocol.md names startup_recovered but does not define the restore handshake strongly enough to prevent silent block-loss or accidental episode reminting
Define startup-recovery handshake ownership in Executor_Protocol.md + Contracts_V0.md
OperationalIdentity block is missing from runtime snapshots in storage-plan.md and Contracts_V0.md
OperationalIdentity must carry: effective_account_id, effective_runtime_id, effective_persona_key, execution_role, actor_kind, requested_account_binding, any_pressure_flags, any_degradation_flags
This block is the single source of effective-identity truth for auditing, receipts, and downstream projections
Retire generic page: string route payload field — it is too coarse for cross-surface navigation and deep-link targeting
Replace all occurrences of bare page: string with the canonical route payload schema (surface_id + object_kind + object_id)
Any existing uses of page: string in cmd.* args or attention item payloads must be migrated
Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md still lacks attempt-level identity, producer attribution, trustworthy cost_usage linkage, and degraded/stale projector behavior
attempt_id is still absent from the canonical artifact ID set even though receipt linkage and the run-graph model now rely on attempt-level identity
runtime-artifact payload ownership is still split across docs without an actually-populated canonical schema family
The attention center cluster requires a canonical record family for project_attention_item

Minimum projection shape: attention_item_id, project_id, severity, owner_kind, reason_code, source_kind, source_object_ref, primary_route_payload, secondary_route_payloads[], display_title, display_subtitle, disclosure_visibility
This record family is absent from storage-plan.md and from Contracts_V0.md
stale_tokens: task_id (in artifact docs, where rewrite needs node_id/package/seam/lane identity)
